Identify the differences between safe and unsafe situations (e.g., bullying, good touch/bad touch, alcohol, tobacco and other drugs, food contamination, poisonous substances);
Know how to access help (e.g., dial 911 in an emergency, trusted adult); and
Describe the influences of media and peer pressure on health.

topics.title: Identify common health issues of children:

subtopics.title: Identify common health issues of children:

outcomes.text: Describe common physical health issues of children in same age group (e.g., intentional and unintentional injury, personal hygiene);
Describe common social health issues of children in same age group (e.g., peer pressure, relationships);
Describe common emotional health issues of children in same age group (e.g., effects of bullying, when family member is sick, sadness, domestic violence); and
Describe common environmental health issues that affect children in same age group (e.g., second-hand smoke, litter, noise).

topics.title: Identify health problems that should be detected and treated early and explain how childhood injuries and illnesses can be prevented or treated:

subtopics.title: Identify health problems that should be detected and treated early and explain how childhood injuries and illnesses can be prevented or treated:

outcomes.text: Describe symptoms of illness (e.g., runny nose, coughing, fever, stomach ache, sadness);
List individuals that can help with detecting and treating childhood injuries and illnesses (e.g., parent, grandparent, teacher, counselor, nurse, doctor);
Describe the benefits of following the directions of health care providers;
Describe safety rules for different situations (e.g., playground safety, bus safety, classroom rules); and
Describe the importance of taking personal responsibility for actions.

units.title: Students will demonstrate the ability to access valid health information and health promoting products and services. Students will:

topics.title: Identify characteristics of valid health information and health promoting products and services:

subtopics.title: Identify characteristics of valid health information and health promoting products and services:

outcomes.text: Identify safe and unsafe products in the home and community (e.g., bleach vs. milk, used needles);
Identify health-promoting products and services (e.g., food choices, community services, physical activity); and
Identify where to seek valid health information (e.g., doctor, dentist, nurse, counselor, appropriate adult).

topics.title: Demonstrate the ability to locate resources from home, school and community that provide valid health information:

subtopics.title: Demonstrate the ability to locate resources from home, school and community that provide valid health information:

outcomes.text: Understand how to use emergency phone numbers (e.g., 911, poison control);
Identify safe adults (e.g., parent, teacher, doctor, dentist, nurse, counselor, appropriate adult);
Recognize unsafe environments/situations; and
Identify where to seek valid health information.

topics.title: Explain how the media influences the selection of health information, products and services:

subtopics.title: Explain how the media influences the selection of health information, products and services:

outcomes.text: Recognize that media messages may be misleading;
Recognize the goals of media (e.g., sell, entertain); and

Recognize media messages that may contain both healthy and unhealthy messages in the areas related to sexuality; nutrition; alcohol, tobacco and other drug use; physical activity; personal safety; mental, social and emotional well-being.

topics.title: Demonstrate the ability to locate school and community health helpers:

subtopics.title: Demonstrate the ability to locate school and community health helpers:

outcomes.text: Recognize safety officials (e.g., police, fire, security, crossing guard); and
Identify safe adults (e.g., parent, teacher, doctor, dentist, nurse, counselor, appropriate adult).

units.title: Students will demonstrate the ability to practice health-enhancing behaviors and reduce health risks. Students will:

topics.title: Identify responsible health behaviors:

subtopics.title: Identify responsible health behaviors:

outcomes.text: Recognize responsible health behaviors in self and others (e.g., personal hygiene, not drinking and driving, daily physical activity, eating fruits and vegetables); and
Demonstrate conflict resolution skills.

topics.title: Identify personal health needs:

subtopics.title: Identify personal health needs:

outcomes.text: Describe where to go when you don't feel good (e.g., parent, teacher, school nurse);
Demonstrate the importance of hygiene (e.g., washing hands to avoid colds); and
Recognize personal safety rules (e.g., don't push others, playground safety, don't go with strangers).

topics.title: Compare behaviors that are safe to those that are risky or harmful:

subtopics.title: Compare behaviors that are safe to those that are risky or harmful:

outcomes.text: Identify when to report dangerous situations to an adult; and

Identify behaviors that are safe and unsafe in the areas related to sexuality; nutrition; alcohol; tobacco and other drug use; physical activity; personal safety; mental, social and emotional well-being.

topics.title: Demonstrate strategies to improve or maintain personal health:

subtopics.title: Demonstrate strategies to improve or maintain personal health:

outcomes.text: Describe ways to improve or maintain personal health in the areas related to sexuality; nutrition; alcohol, tobacco and other drug use; physical activity; personal safety; mental, social and emotional well-being (e.g., eat fruits and vegetables, exercise, don't smoke);
Describe refusal skills in the areas related to sexuality; nutrition; alcohol, tobacco and other drug use; physical activity; personal safety; mental, social and emotional well-being; and

Identify healthy choices in the areas related to sexuality; nutrition, alcohol, tobacco and other drug use; physical activity; personal safety; mental, social and emotional well-being (e.g., walk away from a fight, participate in physical activity, identify healthier foods from a list of foods).

topics.title: Develop injury prevention and management strategies for personal health:

subtopics.title: Develop injury prevention and management strategies for personal health:

outcomes.text: Demonstrate refusal skills in the areas related to sexuality; nutrition; alcohol, tobacco and other drug use; physical activity; personal safety; mental, social and emotional well-being; and
Demonstrate safety rules at home, in school and in the community.

topics.title: Demonstrate ways to avoid and reduce threatening situations:

subtopics.title: Demonstrate ways to avoid and reduce threatening situations:

outcomes.text: Identify trusted adults to go to when faced with a threatening situation.

topics.title: Apply skills to manage stress:

subtopics.title: Apply skills to manage stress:

outcomes.text: Identify situations that cause stress and recognize that stress is not always negative (e.g., bullies, going to a birthday party, reading out loud); and
List activities that help reduce stress (e.g., physical activity, reading).

units.title: Students will analyze the influence of culture, media, technology and other factors on health. Students will:

topics.title: Describe how cultures within the local community influence personal health behaviors:

subtopics.title: Describe how cultures within the local community influence personal health behaviors:

outcomes.text: Recognize similarities and differences in cultures within the community;
Recognize how the media and culture portray gender roles (e.g., pink=girls, blue=boys, short hair vs. long hair, different toys); and

Identify how school and community values relate to health, safety and personal choices in the areas related to sexuality; nutrition; alcohol, tobacco and other drug use; physical activity; personal safety; mental, social and emotional well-being.

topics.title: Explain how media influences thoughts, feelings and health behaviors:

subtopics.title: Explain how media influences thoughts, feelings and health behaviors:

outcomes.text: Identify different forms of media (e.g., television, newspaper, magazines, radio);
Identify the purposes for media (e.g., entertain, sell products, promote services);
Understand that not all media messages are true; and
Recognize how media influences feelings and thoughts.

topics.title: Describe ways technology can influence personal health:

subtopics.title: Describe ways technology can influence personal health:

outcomes.text: Identify different forms of technology (e.g., computers, video games, microwaves, cell phones);
Identify the purposes for technology (e.g., convenience, entertainment, selling products, promoting services); and
Understand that technology affects how we live.

Recognize the purposes for technology in the areas related to sexuality; nutrition; alcohol, tobacco and other drug use; physical activity; personal safety; mental, social and emotional well-being (e.g., medical, conveniences, communication); and

topics.title: Explain how information from school and family influences health:

subtopics.title: Explain how information from school and family influences health:

outcomes.text: List health messages that families give in the areas related to sexuality; nutrition; alcohol, tobacco and other drug use; physical activity; personal safety; mental, social and emotional well-being (e.g., what types of snacks you eat at home, stranger danger, family activities).
List different types of families (e.g., two parents, single parents, extended families).

units.title: Students will demonstrate the ability to use interpersonal communication skills to enhance health. Students will:

topics.title: Distinguish between verbal and non-verbal communication:

subtopics.title: Distinguish between verbal and non-verbal communication:

outcomes.text: Identify the differences between verbal and non-verbal communication;
Describe how people communicate in different ways; and
Recognize different feelings and the verbal and non-verbal forms of communication associated with them.

topics.title: Describe characteristics needed to be a responsible friend and family member:

subtopics.title: Describe characteristics needed to be a responsible friend and family member:

outcomes.text: List ways that a person can show responsibility for his/her own health behaviors.

topics.title: Demonstrate positive ways to express needs, wants and feelings:

subtopics.title: Demonstrate positive ways to express needs, wants and feelings:

outcomes.text: Explain feelings associated with different situations (e.g., conflict - frustration/satisfaction; birthday - happy/excited); and
Explain how to express feelings in a positive way.

topics.title: Demonstrate ways to communicate care, consideration and respect of self and others:

subtopics.title: Demonstrate ways to communicate care, consideration and respect of self and others:

outcomes.text: Demonstrate the ability to appropriately use "I" statements in communication.

topics.title: Demonstrate attentive listening skills to build and maintain health-enhancing relationships:

subtopics.title: Demonstrate attentive listening skills to build and maintain health-enhancing relationships:

outcomes.text: Demonstrate listening skills as a tool to enhance relationships;
Describe when it is appropriate to interrupt for health needs; and
Recognize when someone is telling you to do something that is wrong.

topics.title: Demonstrate refusal skills and explain why they are important to enhance health:

subtopics.title: Demonstrate refusal skills and explain why they are important to enhance health:

outcomes.text: Explain refusal skills in the areas related to sexuality (e.g., good touch/bad touch); nutrition; alcohol, tobacco and other drug use; physical activity; personal safety; mental, social and emotional well being.

topics.title: Differentiate between negative and positive behaviors used in conflict situations:

subtopics.title: Differentiate between negative and positive behaviors used in conflict situations:

outcomes.text: Identify common conflict situations that occur among friends, family members and others;
Describe possible causes of conflict; and
Explain the differences between negative and positive behaviors used in conflict situations.

topics.title: Demonstrate non-violent strategies to resolve conflicts:

subtopics.title: Demonstrate non-violent strategies to resolve conflicts:

outcomes.text: Identify common conflict situations that occur among friends, family members and others; and
Explain non-violent strategies to resolve conflict.

units.title: Students will demonstrate the ability to use goal-setting and decision-making skills to enhance health. Students will:

topics.title: Demonstrate the ability to apply a decision-making process to health issues and problems:

subtopics.title: Demonstrate the ability to apply a decision-making process to health issues and problems:

outcomes.text: Identify actions to make healthy decisions in the areas related to sexuality (e.g., good touch/bad touch); nutrition; alcohol, tobacco and other drug use; physical activity; personal safety; mental, social and emotional well-being.

topics.title: Explain when to ask for assistance in making health-related decisions and setting health goals:

subtopics.title: Explain when to ask for assistance in making health-related decisions and setting health goals:

outcomes.text: Identify when it is appropriate to ask for help in making health-related decisions (e.g., when you are lost, when being bullied).

topics.title: Predict outcomes of positive health decisions:

subtopics.title: Predict outcomes of positive health decisions:

outcomes.text: Describe how decisions affect health in the areas related to sexuality; nutrition; alcohol, tobacco and other drug use; physical activity; personal safety; mental, social and emotional well-being (e.g., eating right and exercising leads to healthy development).

topics.title: Set a personal health goal and track progress toward achievement:

subtopics.title: Set a personal health goal and track progress toward achievement:

outcomes.text: Identify a personal health goal in one of the areas related to sexuality; nutrition; alcohol, tobacco and other drug use; physical activity; personal safety; mental, social and emotional well-being.

units.title: Students will demonstrate the ability to advocate for personal, family, peer and community health. Students will:

topics.title: Describe a variety of methods to convey accurate health information and ideas:

subtopics.title: Describe a variety of methods to convey accurate health information and ideas:

outcomes.text: Recognize methods to convey accurate health information and ideas.

topics.title: Express information and opinions about health issues:

subtopics.title: Express information and opinions about health issues:

outcomes.text: Discuss when it is appropriate to express opinions about health issues.

topics.title: Identify community agencies/resources that advocate for healthy individuals, families, peers and communities:

subtopics.title: Identify community agencies/resources that advocate for healthy individuals, families, peers and communities:

outcomes.text: List places and people in the school and community you can go to for health information (e.g., school nurse, doctor's office).

topics.title: Demonstrate the ability to influence and support others in making health-enhancing choices:

subtopics.title: Demonstrate the ability to influence and support others in making health-enhancing choices:

outcomes.text: List ways to help others make healthy choices.
